The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	package chainledger
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"sort"
7		"unicode/utf8"
8	)
9	
10	// lineageExportEdge is one direct dependency in an exported lineage document,
11	// written in the actual derivation direction: From is the upstream dataset and
12	// To is the dataset derived from it.
13	type lineageExportEdge struct {
14		From string `json:"from"`
15		To   string `json:"to"`
16	}
17	
18	// lineageExportDocument is the JSON shape produced by the lineage exports:
19	// the set of dataset names involved in the requested derivation, plus every
20	// direct dependency between them.
21	type lineageExportDocument struct {
22		Nodes []string            `json:"nodes"`
23		Edges []lineageExportEdge `json:"edges"`
24	}
25	
26	// ExportUpstreamLineage exports the complete upstream lineage of target as a
27	// JSON document, for other programs to consume. Where Upstreams explains each
28	// source with a single shortest path, this export preserves every branch the
29	// target actually depends on: even when a source already reaches the target
30	// directly, the longer routes through intermediate datasets stay in the
31	// document.
32	//
33	// The document's top level holds two arrays:
34	//
35	//   - "nodes": the names of target itself and every direct and indirect
36	//     upstream of it, each exactly once, ordered by Go string order.
37	//   - "edges": every direct dependency between the included nodes, each
38	//     exactly once, written {"from": upstream, "to": derived} in the actual
39	//     derivation direction and ordered by "from" and then "to", again in Go
40	//     string order.
41	//
42	// The target's downstreams and datasets that take no part in its derivation
43	// never appear. A target with no upstreams exports successfully with itself
44	// as the only node and an empty (non-null) edges array. The ordering is fully
45	// determined by the names, so neither registration order nor the stored
46	// upstream list order can change the output; names are matched by exact
47	// registered value (case-sensitive) and written verbatim, with JSON escaping
48	// applied so a reader recovers the original bytes.
49	//
50	// Every name in the exported set must be valid UTF-8: JSON cannot carry an
51	// invalid byte sequence losslessly (a JSON encoder would replace it with the
52	// replacement character and two distinct names could collapse into one), so a
53	// success guarantees the reader recovers every name exactly as registered. If
54	// any included node's name is not valid UTF-8, the whole export fails; the
55	// error identifies the offending name in Go-quoted form (%q), which renders
56	// each non-displayable byte as its own \xNN escape, so different bad bytes
57	// never share one replacement glyph. When several names are invalid, the one
58	// sorting first in Go string order is reported, keeping the error independent
59	// of registration and stored-list order. Only the target and its ancestors are
60	// inspected: an unrelated dataset or a downstream of the target may hold an
61	// invalid name without blocking this export. A real replacement character
62	// (U+FFFD) that is itself part of a name is valid UTF-8 and exports normally.
63	//
64	// The export is read-only: it changes no node, edge or stored list order. An
65	// empty target is rejected as a missing name; a target absent from the graph
66	// (including an empty or nil graph) is rejected with an error naming it, and
67	// those checks take precedence over name encoding. Failures return an empty
68	// string and never a partial document.
69	func ExportUpstreamLineage(graph map[string]*Lineage, target string) (string, error) {
70		if target == "" {
71			return "", errInvalid("dataset name is required")
72		}
73		if _, ok := graph[target]; !ok {
74			return "", errInvalid("dataset not found: " + target)
75		}
76	
77		return renderLineageExport(graph, ancestorClosure(graph, target))
78	}
79	
80	// ExportSourceTargetLineage exports only the part of target's upstream lineage
81	// that a specified registered source actually participates in, as a JSON
82	// document for other programs to consume. Where ExportUpstreamLineage brings
83	// along every source target depends on, this scoped export answers just "how
84	// does this one source derive this target".
85	//
86	// The document holds exactly the datasets that lie on at least one existing
87	// derivation route from source to target — source and target included — and
88	// exactly the direct dependencies carried by those routes. Concretely a node
89	// is included when it is both a direct or indirect downstream of source and a
90	// direct or indirect upstream of target; an edge is included when both of its
91	// endpoints are. Every node and edge appears once. Keeping the full node set
92	// (rather than one picked path) preserves every branch simultaneously: if
93	// source reaches target directly, through a, and through b and mid, limiting
94	// the export to source and report still keeps all three routes complete — a
95	// longer route is never dropped because a direct relation or a shorter route
96	// exists.
97	//
98	// What stays out follows from the same intersection:
99	//
100	//   - An independent source that feeds an included intermediate dataset but is
101	//     not itself downstream of source is excluded, and so is the edge from it:
102	//     if a additionally depends on extra, neither extra nor extra -> a appears.
103	//   - A downstream of source that cannot reach target is excluded; ancestors
104	//     of source and downstreams of target are excluded as well.
105	//
106	// When source and target are the same registered dataset, that dataset alone
107	// is exported with an empty edges array. When both are registered but no
108	// derivation route from source to target exists, the export still succeeds but
109	// holds two empty (non-null) arrays — no isolated endpoint is retained, and a
110	// dependency running the other way (target derives source) is not treated as
111	// reachability.
112	//
113	// The document shape, the {"from": upstream, "to": derived} edge direction,
114	// the nodes-by-name and edges-by-from-then-to Go-string ordering, the
115	// byte-exact name handling and the invalid-UTF-8 failure rule all match
116	// ExportUpstreamLineage, judged over the scoped node set only: a name outside
117	// the selected routes, including one on target's other ancestry, never blocks
118	// this export. Output is therefore fully determined by the registered names
119	// and independent of registration order and stored upstream-list order.
120	//
121	// Names match by exact registered value (case-sensitive). Source is validated
122	// first: an empty name is a missing-name error and an unregistered name
123	// (including against an empty or nil graph) is an error naming it; only then
124	// is target checked the same way. Those checks take precedence over name
125	// encoding. The export is read-only — it changes no node, bidirectional
126	// relationship or stored list order — and any failure returns an empty
127	// string, never a partial document.
128	func ExportSourceTargetLineage(graph map[string]*Lineage, source, target string) (string, error) {
129		if source == "" {
130			return "", errInvalid("dataset name is required")
131		}
132		if _, ok := graph[source]; !ok {
133			return "", errInvalid("dataset not found: " + source)
134		}
135		if target == "" {
136			return "", errInvalid("dataset name is required")
137		}
138		if _, ok := graph[target]; !ok {
139			return "", errInvalid("dataset not found: " + target)
140		}
141	
142		// A node belongs to a source -> target derivation exactly when it is
143		// downstream of source AND upstream of target. Register rejects cycles, so
144		// both walks terminate; the visited sets guard the loops regardless.
145		downstream := descendantClosure(graph, source)
146		upstream := ancestorClosure(graph, target)
147		included := make(map[string]bool)
148		for name := range downstream {
149			if upstream[name] {
150				included[name] = true
151			}
152		}
153	
154		return renderLineageExport(graph, included)
155	}
156	
157	// ancestorClosure collects start and every dataset reachable from it by
158	// following parent edges.
159	func ancestorClosure(graph map[string]*Lineage, start string) map[string]bool {
160		included := map[string]bool{start: true}
161		queue := []string{start}
162		for len(queue) > 0 {
163			node := queue[0]
164			queue = queue[1:]
165			for _, parent := range graph[node].Parents {
166				if !included[parent] {
167					included[parent] = true
168					queue = append(queue, parent)
169				}
170			}
171		}
172		return included
173	}
174	
175	// descendantClosure collects start and every dataset reachable from it by
176	// following child edges.
177	func descendantClosure(graph map[string]*Lineage, start string) map[string]bool {
178		included := map[string]bool{start: true}
179		queue := []string{start}
180		for len(queue) > 0 {
181			node := queue[0]
182			queue = queue[1:]
183			for _, child := range graph[node].Children {
184				if !included[child] {
185					included[child] = true
186					queue = append(queue, child)
187				}
188			}
189		}
190		return included
191	}
192	
193	// renderLineageExport serializes one already-decided node set in the single
194	// document format shared by the lineage exports.
195	func renderLineageExport(graph map[string]*Lineage, included map[string]bool) (string, error) {
196		nodes := make([]string, 0, len(included))
197		for name := range included {
198			nodes = append(nodes, name)
199		}
200		sort.Strings(nodes)
201	
202		// JSON text must round-trip every name byte for byte. encoding/json would
203		// silently rewrite an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence into U+FFFD rather than
204		// fail, and two byte-different names could then decode to the same value,
205		// so check the included names ourselves before any document is produced.
206		// Nodes are already in Go string order, so the first invalid one is the
207		// deterministic answer regardless of registration or upstream-list order;
208		// %q exposes the actual bytes (non-displayable ones as \xNN) instead of a
209		// shared replacement glyph. Nodes outside the selected set are never
210		// examined.
211		for _, name := range nodes {
212			if !utf8.ValidString(name) {
213				return "", errInvalid(fmt.Sprintf(
214					"dataset name is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be exported losslessly: %q", name))
215			}
216		}
217	
218		// Every direct dependency between included nodes is an edge. In the full
219		// upstream export every parent of an included node is included by
220		// construction; in a source-scoped export an included intermediate node may
221		// also depend on an independent, excluded source, so the parent has to be
222		// checked against the set. The dedupe set guards the one-edge-once rule even
223		// if a stored list ever repeated a name.
224		edges := make([]lineageExportEdge, 0)
225		seen := make(map[lineageExportEdge]bool)
226		for _, name := range nodes {
227			for _, parent := range graph[name].Parents {
228				if !included[parent] {
229					continue
230				}
231				edge := lineageExportEdge{From: parent, To: name}
232				if !seen[edge] {
233					seen[edge] = true
234					edges = append(edges, edge)
235				}
236			}
237		}
238		sort.Slice(edges, func(i, j int) bool {
239			if edges[i].From != edges[j].From {
240				return edges[i].From < edges[j].From
241			}
242			return edges[i].To < edges[j].To
243		})
244	
245		data, err := json.Marshal(lineageExportDocument{Nodes: nodes, Edges: edges})
246		if err != nil {
247			return "", err
248		}
249		return string(data), nil
250	}

11	// ImportLineage decodes a lineage document in the same JSON shape the exports
12	// produce and returns a brand-new, independent lineage graph holding exactly
13	// the document's nodes and direct dependencies. The returned map works with
14	// every existing operation: Register, Rename, Unregister, Impacts,
15	// ImpactsWithCutoffs, Upstreams, CommonUpstreams, Roots and both exports. The
16	// caller's own graph is never read or modified — import only creates a new map.
17	//
18	// The document is one single JSON object with two array fields:
19	//
20	//   - "nodes": dataset names. Every listed node exists in the new graph,
21	//     including independent datasets with no dependency in either direction.
22	//     A name listed more than once counts once.
23	//   - "edges": direct dependencies written {"from": upstream, "to": derived},
24	//     the same direction the exports use. Each edge becomes the derived
25	//     dataset's direct upstream (Parents) and, mirrored, the upstream's direct
26	//     downstream (Children). The same dependency listed more than once counts
27	//     once. The endpoint fields are recognized by their exact decoded key
28	//     name: only keys that decode to precisely "from" and "to" (any JSON
29	//     escape spelling included) set the endpoints. Case variants such as
30	//     "From" or "TO" are unknown fields — ignored like any other unknown
31	//     field, their values never validated or used — so an edge carrying only
32	//     a case variant is rejected as missing that endpoint.
33	//
34	// Import scope is exactly the document: nothing is invented, inferred or
35	// completed. A document produced by a source-scoped export rebuilds only that
36	// part of the lineage — other sources and downstreams the export omitted are
37	// not restored. Direct relations and longer branches through intermediate
38	// nodes are kept together, so explanation paths are still chosen by the
39	// existing query rules (fewest edges, then the lexicographically smallest full
40	// path in Go string order).
41	//
42	// Nodes and edges may appear in the document in any order; the result is
43	// independent of that order. Every node's direct upstream and downstream
44	// lists are stored in Go string order, so a graph imported from a valid export
45	// document re-exports byte-identical text for the same target or source-target
46	// pair.
47	//
48	// Names are identified by their exact decoded JSON value: matching is
49	// case-sensitive and spaces, Chinese characters, quotes, backslashes and
50	// newlines are preserved verbatim — never trimmed or rewritten. The input
51	// must be valid UTF-8 and hold exactly one complete JSON object; "nodes" and
52	// "edges" must both be present, each as an array of the correct element type
53	// (null is not an array). Two empty arrays import successfully as an empty,
54	// ready-to-register graph.
55	//
56	// The whole document is validated before the graph is returned, so every
57	// failure yields a nil graph and an error describing the document problem,
58	// never a partial graph:
59	//
60	//   - Empty or whitespace-only text, text that is not valid UTF-8, malformed
61	//     JSON, more than one JSON value, a non-object document, a duplicated
62	//     object key, a missing or null array, or an element of the wrong type is
63	//     rejected.
64	//   - An empty node name is rejected as a missing name.
65	//   - A name (a node name, or an edge's "from" or "to") containing an unpaired
66	//     Unicode surrogate escape is rejected. encoding/json rewrites a lone
67	//     \uD800–\uDFFF escape to the replacement character U+FFFD, so two
68	//     different bad names would silently collapse into one "�" and a bad edge
69	//     endpoint could match a real dataset named "�". A high-surrogate escape
70	//     is valid only immediately followed by the low-surrogate escape that
71	//     completes one character; a lone high, a lone low, a reversed pair, or a
72	//     pair broken by other characters or escapes is unpaired. The error says
73	//     so, names where the escape was found (node name, edge "from" or edge
74	//     "to") and quotes the offending escape in its original \uXXXX spelling,
75	//     so distinct bad names never share one replacement glyph. A real U+FFFD
76	//     character written directly or as a \uFFFD escape is valid, as is a
77	//     correctly paired \uD83D\uDE00: both spellings decode to the same one
78	//     character as a literal emoji, so a node written one way and an edge the
79	//     other still connect. The document text "\\uD800" (an escaped backslash
80	//     followed by letters) is an ordinary name containing no surrogate escape
81	//     and is kept verbatim.
82	//   - Both endpoints of every edge must be listed in nodes; an edge naming a
83	//     dataset the document does not list fails the whole import, and the error
84	//     names that dataset. Edges missing an endpoint are rejected the same way.
85	//   - A self-dependency or a dependency cycle of any length fails the whole
86	//     import; the error states that the lineage contains a cycle and names the
87	//     datasets on it.
88	func ImportLineage(text string) (map[string]*Lineage, error) {
89		nodesRaw, edgesRaw, err := decodeLineageDocument(text)
90		if err != nil {
91			return nil, err
92		}
93	
94		var nodeItems []json.RawMessage
95		if err := json.Unmarshal(nodesRaw, &nodeItems); err != nil {
96			return nil, errInvalid("lineage document nodes must be an array of JSON strings: " + err.Error())
97		}
98		var edgeItems []json.RawMessage
99		if err := json.Unmarshal(edgesRaw, &edgeItems); err != nil {
100			return nil, errInvalid(`lineage document edges must be an array of {"from": ..., "to": ...} objects: ` + err.Error())
101		}
102	
103		// Build the de-duplicated node set. Each element must itself be a JSON
104		// string (null is not a name). Names keep their exact decoded value: the
105		// document was already checked to be valid UTF-8, so every decoded name is
106		// the original value, with JSON unescaping applied (quotes, backslashes,
107		// newlines and all). Unpaired \u surrogate escapes are rejected on the raw
108		// text first: encoding/json accepts them and rewrites each one to U+FFFD,
109		// so two different bad names would silently collapse into one.
110		nodes := make(map[string]bool, len(nodeItems))
111		for _, item := range nodeItems {
112			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(item))
113			if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, `"`) {
114				return nil, errInvalid("lineage document nodes must be an array of JSON strings")
115			}
116			name, err := unmarshalLineageName(item)
117			if err != nil {
118				return nil, err
119			}
120			if name == "" {
121				return nil, errInvalid("dataset name is required")
122			}
123			nodes[name] = true
124		}
125	
126		// Resolve every edge before constructing entries. Each element must be a
127		// {"from": ..., "to": ...} object; both endpoints must be listed nodes.
128		// De-duplicated dependencies only, independent of document order.
129		dependencies := make(map[lineageExportEdge]bool, len(edgeItems))
130		for _, item := range edgeItems {
131			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(item))
132			if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "{") {
133				return nil, errInvalid(`lineage document edges must be an array of {"from": ..., "to": ...} objects`)
134			}
135			// Decode the object structurally without accepting endpoint strings:
136			// the from/to values are then validated as names themselves, so an
137			// unpaired surrogate escape in an endpoint fails the import instead of
138			// silently matching a real "�" dataset. Keys are matched by their exact
139			// decoded name through a map: only fields literally named "from" and
140			// "to" (however escaped in the raw text) set the endpoints. A struct
141			// unmarshal would also bind case variants like "From" or "FROM" to the
142			// endpoint fields, letting an unknown field overwrite the declared
143			// endpoints depending on member order; here they are unknown fields
144			// like any other and their values never participate in the lineage.
145			var edgeRaw map[string]json.RawMessage
146			if err := json.Unmarshal(item, &edgeRaw); err != nil {
147				return nil, errInvalid(`lineage document edges must be an array of {"from": ..., "to": ...} objects: ` + err.Error())
148			}
149			from, err := unmarshalEndpointName(edgeRaw["from"], "from")
150			if err != nil {
151				return nil, err
152			}
153			to, err := unmarshalEndpointName(edgeRaw["to"], "to")
154			if err != nil {
155				return nil, err
156			}
157			edge := lineageExportEdge{From: from, To: to}
158			if edge.From == "" {
159				return nil, errInvalid(`lineage document edge is missing its upstream endpoint ("from")`)
160			}
161			if edge.To == "" {
162				return nil, errInvalid(`lineage document edge is missing its derived endpoint ("to")`)
163			}
164			if !nodes[edge.From] {
165				return nil, errInvalid("edge endpoint not listed in nodes: " + edge.From)
166			}
167			if !nodes[edge.To] {
168				return nil, errInvalid("edge endpoint not listed in nodes: " + edge.To)
169			}
170			dependencies[edge] = true
171		}
172	
173		// Materialize the new graph with direct lists in Go string order. All
174		// entries exist before any edge is attached, and a rejected import returns
175		// nil, so a caller can never observe a partially filled graph.
176		graph := make(map[string]*Lineage, len(nodes))
177		for name := range nodes {
178			graph[name] = &Lineage{Dataset: name}
179		}
180		for edge := range dependencies {
181			graph[edge.To].Parents = append(graph[edge.To].Parents, edge.From)
182			graph[edge.From].Children = append(graph[edge.From].Children, edge.To)
183		}
184		for _, entry := range graph {
185			sort.Strings(entry.Parents)
186			sort.Strings(entry.Children)
187		}

189		// Cycles of any length (self dependencies included) are rejected with the
190		// datasets on one such cycle named deterministically.
191		if cycle := findLineageCycle(graph); cycle != nil {
192			return nil, errInvalid("lineage contains a cycle: " + strings.Join(cycle, " -> "))
193		}
194		return graph, nil
195	}

197	// decodeLineageDocument runs the document-level checks and returns the raw
198	// JSON values of the nodes and edges arrays: the text must be non-empty, valid
199	// UTF-8, exactly one complete JSON object with no duplicated object key, and
200	// both fields must be present as arrays (null rejected, element types are
201	// checked by the caller's typed unmarshal).
202	func decodeLineageDocument(text string) (json.RawMessage, json.RawMessage, error) {
203		if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
204			return nil, nil, errInvalid("lineage document is empty: expected one JSON object with nodes and edges arrays")
205		}
206		// encoding/json silently rewrites invalid UTF-8 into U+FFFD instead of
207		// failing, and two byte-different names could then collapse into one, so
208		// the whole text is checked before anything is decoded.
209		if !utf8.ValidString(text) {
210			return nil, nil, errInvalid("lineage document is not valid UTF-8")
211		}
212		if err := rejectDuplicateKeys(text); err != nil {
213			return nil, nil, err
214		}
215	
216		var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
217		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(text), &raw); err != nil {
218			return nil, nil, errInvalid("lineage document must be one complete JSON object: " + err.Error())
219		}
220	
221		nodes, ok := raw["nodes"]
222		if !ok {
223			return nil, nil, errInvalid(`lineage document is missing the "nodes" array`)
224		}
225		edges, ok := raw["edges"]
226		if !ok {
227			return nil, nil, errInvalid(`lineage document is missing the "edges" array`)
228		}
229		if err := requireJSONArray(nodes, "nodes"); err != nil {
230			return nil, nil, err
231		}
232		if err := requireJSONArray(edges, "edges"); err != nil {
233			return nil, nil, err
234		}
235		return nodes, edges, nil
236	}

238	// requireJSONArray rejects a field that is null or whose value is not a JSON
239	// array; element types inside the array are validated by typed unmarshalling.
240	func requireJSONArray(raw json.RawMessage, field string) error {
241		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
242		switch {
243		case trimmed == "null":
244			return errInvalid("lineage document field " + field + " must be an array, got null")
245		case !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "["):
246			return errInvalid("lineage document field " + field + " must be an array")
247		}
248		return nil
249	}

251	// decodeLineageName decodes one JSON string token (a node name or an edge
252	// endpoint) into its exact Go value, rejecting unpaired \u surrogate escapes
253	// before json.Unmarshal can touch the text.
254	//
255	// encoding/json accepts a lone \uD800–\uDFFF escape and rewrites it to the
256	// replacement character U+FFFD: two byte-different bad names would then
257	// collapse into one "�", and a bad edge endpoint would silently match a real
258	// dataset named "�". The raw token is therefore scanned first. A high
259	// surrogate escape is valid only when it is immediately followed by the low
260	// surrogate escape that together represent one character; a lone high, a lone
261	// low, a reversed pair, or a pair broken by other escapes or characters is
262	// unpaired. On success ok is true with the decoded value; when the token
263	// contains an unpaired escape, ok is still true, name is empty and badEscape
264	// holds the escape in its original \uXXXX spelling; ok is false only when the
265	// token is not a JSON string. The token was extracted from an already
266	// validated document, so json.Unmarshal cannot fail for a token that starts
267	// with a quote.
268	func decodeLineageName(raw json.RawMessage) (name, badEscape string, ok bool) {
269		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(string(raw)), `"`) {
270			return "", "", false
271		}
272		if bad := firstUnpairedSurrogate(string(raw)); bad != "" {
273			return "", bad, true
274		}
275		var decoded string
276		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &decoded); err != nil {
277			return "", "", false
278		}
279		return decoded, "", true
280	}

282	// firstUnpairedSurrogate scans the raw text of one JSON string token and
283	// returns the first unpaired \u surrogate escape in its original spelling
284	// ("" when every surrogate escape is correctly paired). Escaped backslashes
285	// are skipped as a unit, so "\\ud800" is literal backslash-plus-letters, not a
286	// surrogate escape.
287	func firstUnpairedSurrogate(token string) string {
288		for i := 0; i < len(token); {
289			if token[i] != '\\' {
290				i++
291				continue
292			}
293			if i+1 >= len(token) {
294				i++
295				continue
296			}
297			switch token[i+1] {
298			case '\\':
299				// An escaped backslash consumes both characters; whatever follows
300				// is literal text, including a "\ud800"-looking sequence.
301				i += 2
302				continue
303			case 'u':
304				r, valid := decodeJSONHexU(token, i)
305				if !valid {
306					i += 2 // malformed token; the document-level decode already rejected it
307					continue
308				}
309				switch {
310				case r >= 0xDC00 && r <= 0xDFFF:
311					return token[i : i+6] // lone low surrogate
312				case r >= 0xD800 && r <= 0xDBFF:
313					// A high surrogate is valid only when the very next token is a
314					// low surrogate escape; any other escape, character or end of
315					// string leaves it unpaired.
316					next, nextValid := decodeJSONHexU(token, i+6)
317					if !nextValid || next < 0xDC00 || next > 0xDFFF {
318						return token[i : i+6]
319					}
320					i += 12
321					continue
322				}
323				i += 6
324				continue
325			}
326			i += 2 // any other JSON escape (\", \n, \t, ...)
327		}
328		return ""
329	}

331	// decodeJSONHexU decodes the \uXXXX escape beginning at token[pos] (token[pos]
332	// is a backslash and token[pos+1] the letter u) into its code point.
333	func decodeJSONHexU(token string, pos int) (rune, bool) {
334		if pos+6 > len(token) || token[pos] != '\\' || token[pos+1] != 'u' {
335			return 0, false
336		}
337		var r rune
338		for k := pos + 2; k < pos+6; k++ {
339			var digit rune
340			switch {
341			case token[k] >= '0' && token[k] <= '9':
342				digit = rune(token[k] - '0')
343			case token[k] >= 'a' && token[k] <= 'f':
344				digit = rune(token[k]-'a') + 10
345			case token[k] >= 'A' && token[k] <= 'F':
346				digit = rune(token[k]-'A') + 10
347			default:
348				return 0, false
349			}
350			r = r*16 + digit
351		}
352		return r, true
353	}

355	// unmarshalLineageName decodes one nodes-array element that already passed the
356	// string-token guard. An unpaired surrogate fails the whole import with an
357	// error that says the node name held an unpaired surrogate escape and quotes
358	// the escape in its original \uXXXX spelling.
359	func unmarshalLineageName(raw json.RawMessage) (string, error) {
360		name, badEscape, ok := decodeLineageName(raw)
361		if !ok {
362			return "", errInvalid("lineage document nodes must be an array of JSON strings")
363		}
364		if badEscape != "" {
365			return "", errInvalid("lineage document node name contains an unpaired Unicode surrogate escape '" +
366				badEscape + "'; surrogate escapes are valid only as a matched " +
367				`\uXXXX\uYYYY high-low pair`)
368		}
369		return name, nil
370	}

373	// or null value returns "" like an absent field so the existing
374	// missing-endpoint checks report it; a present non-string value keeps the
375	// edges type error; an unpaired surrogate fails the import, naming the
376	// endpoint it came from and quoting the original escape.
377	func unmarshalEndpointName(raw json.RawMessage, endpoint string) (string, error) {
378		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
379		if trimmed == "" || trimmed == "null" {
380			return "", nil
381		}
382		name, badEscape, ok := decodeLineageName(raw)
383		if !ok {
384			return "", errInvalid(`lineage document edges must be an array of {"from": ..., "to": ...} objects: ` +
385				`endpoint "` + endpoint + `" must be a JSON string`)
386		}
387		if badEscape != "" {
388			return "", errInvalid(`lineage document edge "` + endpoint + `" endpoint contains an ` +
389				"unpaired Unicode surrogate escape '" + badEscape +
390				"'; surrogate escapes are valid only as a matched " +
391				`\uXXXX\uYYYY high-low pair`)
392		}
393		return name, nil

396	// objectFrame tracks one container during the structural key scan: whether it
397	// is an object (arrays need no key tracking), whether the next string token is
398	// that object's key, and the keys already seen in it.
399	type objectFrame struct {
400		object    bool
401		expectKey bool
402		keys      map[string]bool
403	}
404	
405	// rejectDuplicateKeys tokenizes the text and rejects any JSON object that
406	// repeats a key, any document whose top-level value is not an object, and any
407	// trailing JSON value after the closing object. encoding/json accepts all
408	// three silently (last key wins; null decodes into a map as no value at all;
409	// trailing values are rejected by Unmarshal but with a generic message), so
410	// the explicit scan makes document problems deterministic.
411	func rejectDuplicateKeys(text string) error {
412		dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(text))
413		// Numbers are only structure here, never values: keep them as raw
414		// json.Number literals so a syntactically valid number of any magnitude
415		// (1e400, a hundred-digit integer) tokenizes without a float64 range
416		// error. The scanner still validates the literal itself, so 01, 1e or
417		// NaN remain malformed JSON and fail the document.
418		dec.UseNumber()
419		var stack []objectFrame
420		rootClosed := false
421		for {
422			tok, err := dec.Token()
423			if err == io.EOF {
424				if len(stack) != 0 || !rootClosed {
425					return errInvalid("lineage document must be one complete JSON object")
426				}
427				return nil
428			}
429			// Anything at all after the root object closes is a second value or
430			// garbage, whether tokenized as a token or as a scan error.
431			if rootClosed {
432				return errInvalid("lineage document must hold exactly one JSON object")
433			}
434			if err != nil {
435				return errInvalid("lineage document must be one complete JSON object: " + err.Error())
436			}
437	
438			switch t := tok.(type) {
439			case json.Delim:
440				switch t {
441				case '{':
442					stack = append(stack, objectFrame{object: true, expectKey: true, keys: map[string]bool{}})
443				case '[':
444					if len(stack) == 0 {
445						return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays, got an array")
446					}
447					stack = append(stack, objectFrame{})
448				case '}', ']':
449					if len(stack) == 0 {
450						return errInvalid("lineage document has an unmatched " + string(t))
451					}
452					stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
453					if len(stack) == 0 {
454						if t != '}' {
455							return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays")
456						}
457						rootClosed = true
458					} else if stack[len(stack)-1].object {
459						// A nested container was this object member's value; the
460						// next member, if any, starts with a key.
461						stack[len(stack)-1].expectKey = true
462					}
463				}
464			case string:
465				if len(stack) == 0 {
466					return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays, got a string")
467				}
468				top := &stack[len(stack)-1]
469				if !top.object {
470					continue // string element of an array; members are delimiter-tracked
471				}
472				if !top.expectKey {
473					top.expectKey = true // string value consumed; a key may follow
474					continue
475				}
476				if top.keys[t] {
477					return errInvalid("lineage document contains a duplicated object key: " + t)
478				}
479				top.keys[t] = true
480				top.expectKey = false
481			default: // number, bool, nil
482				if len(stack) == 0 {
483					return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays")
484				}
485				if stack[len(stack)-1].object {
486					stack[len(stack)-1].expectKey = true
487				}
488			}
489		}
490	}

492	// findLineageCycle returns the datasets on one directed cycle written in the
493	// actual derivation direction (upstream -> derived), with the smallest-named
494	// dataset on the cycle first and repeated last, or nil when the graph is
495	// acyclic. Every node on a cycle reaches itself by following parent edges, so
496	// a depth-first walk with a per-path stack catches a back edge of any length,
497	// including a self dependency. Nodes are visited in Go string order and parent
498	// lists are already sorted, so the reported cycle is independent of the
499	// document's node and edge ordering.
500	func findLineageCycle(graph map[string]*Lineage) []string {
501		color := make(map[string]int, len(graph)) // 0 unseen, 1 on current path, 2 done
502		var stack []string
503		var found []string
504	
505		var visit func(node string) bool
506		visit = func(node string) bool {
507			color[node] = 1
508			stack = append(stack, node)
509			for _, parent := range graph[node].Parents {
510				switch color[parent] {
511				case 0:
512					if visit(parent) {
513						return true
514					}
515				case 1:
516					// A back edge to a node on the current path closes a cycle:
517					// parent ... node, with node deriving from parent.
518					start := 0
519					for stack[start] != parent {
520						start++
521					}
522					found = append([]string(nil), stack[start:]...)
523					return true
524				}
525			}
526			stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
527			color[node] = 2
528			return false
529		}
530	
531		names := make([]string, 0, len(graph))
532		for name := range graph {
533			names = append(names, name)
534		}
535		sort.Strings(names)
536		for _, name := range names {
537			if color[name] == 0 && visit(name) {
538				return derivationCycle(found)
539			}
540		}
541		return nil
542	}

544	// derivationCycle converts a closed cycle segment discovered while following
545	// parent edges into the derivation direction, then rotates it so the
546	// smallest-named dataset comes first (and stays last). A parent-direction
547	// segment [p0, p1, ..., pk] closes with pk deriving from p0, so the derivation
548	// runs p0 -> pk -> ... -> p1 -> p0.
549	func derivationCycle(parentPath []string) []string {
550		body := make([]string, 0, len(parentPath)+1)
551		body = append(body, parentPath[0])
552		for i := len(parentPath) - 1; i >= 1; i-- {
553			body = append(body, parentPath[i])
554		}
555	
556		min := 0
557		for i := 1; i < len(body); i++ {
558			if body[i] < body[min] {
559				min = i
560			}
561		}
562		rotated := make([]string, 0, len(body)+1)
563		rotated = append(rotated, body[min:]...)
564		rotated = append(rotated, body[:min]...)
565		rotated = append(rotated, body[min])
566		return rotated
567	}

1	// Package chainledger implements the on-chain data governance core.
2	package chainledger
3	
4	import "sort"
5	
6	// Dataset is one ingestible on-chain data source with a declared schema version.
7	type Dataset struct {
8		Name          string
9		SchemaVersion int
10		Rows          int
11		Upstreams     []string
12	}
13	
14	// Lineage records where a dataset came from, so every derived table can be traced.
15	type Lineage struct {
16		Dataset  string
17		Parents  []string
18		Children []string
19	}
20	
21	// Register links a dataset into the lineage graph and rejects cycles.
22	//
23	// Re-registering an existing dataset replaces its direct upstreams with parents
24	// (de-duplicated, first occurrence wins, list order preserved) while keeping its
25	// existing direct downstreams. Reverse edges stay consistent: upstreams removed
26	// from the list drop the dataset from their children, newly added upstreams gain
27	// it at the end of their children, and retained upstreams keep exactly one entry
28	// in its original position.
29	//
30	// The whole request is validated before the graph is touched, so a rejected
31	// registration leaves every node, edge and ordering untouched. The parents slice
32	// is copied: mutating it after Register returns does not affect the graph.
33	func Register(graph map[string]*Lineage, dataset Dataset, parents []string) error {
34		if dataset.Name == "" {
35			return errInvalid("dataset name is required")
36		}
37	
38		// Validate up front, walking the request in input order so the first problem
39		// encountered is the one reported. No graph mutation happens in this loop.
40		upstreams := make([]string, 0, len(parents))
41		known := map[string]bool{}
42		// All cycle checks in this one request share a single memoized walk over the
43		// graph as it stands now: probe records whether each visited node can reach
44		// dataset.Name through existing parent edges. Candidate upstreams that come
45		// from the same source or merge repeatedly (diamonds) then traverse the
46		// shared lineage once instead of re-walking it per candidate. The recorded
47		// conclusion is a property of the current graph, so it is never reused
48		// across registrations.
49		probe := newAncestorProbe(graph, dataset.Name)
50		for _, parent := range parents {
51			if parent == dataset.Name {
52				return errInvalid("dataset " + dataset.Name + " cannot be its own parent")
53			}
54			if _, ok := graph[parent]; !ok {
55				return errInvalid("unknown parent " + parent)
56			}
57			// A new edge dataset -> parent closes a cycle exactly when parent can
58			// already reach dataset through existing parent edges. This covers
59			// transitive paths of any depth, not only direct mutual references;
60			// shared ancestors and diamond merges read as the benign merges they are
61			// unless a branch genuinely leads back to dataset.
62			if probe.canReach(parent) {
63				return errInvalid("cycle through " + parent + " for dataset " + dataset.Name)
64			}
65			if !known[parent] {
66				known[parent] = true
67				upstreams = append(upstreams, parent)
68			}
69		}
70	
71		entry, existed := graph[dataset.Name]
72		if !existed {
73			entry = &Lineage{Dataset: dataset.Name}
74		}
75	
76		// Remove reverse edges from upstreams the dataset no longer declares.
77		for _, old := range entry.Parents {
78			if known[old] {
79				continue
80			}
81			if p, ok := graph[old]; ok {
82				p.Children = removeChild(p.Children, dataset.Name)
83			}
84		}
85	
86		// Mirror every declared upstream exactly once. An existing edge keeps its
87		// position; a missing edge is appended after the current children.
88		for _, parent := range upstreams {
89			graph[parent].Children = addChildOnce(graph[parent].Children, dataset.Name)
90		}
91	
92		entry.Parents = upstreams
93		if !existed {
94			graph[dataset.Name] = entry
95		}
96		return nil
97	}

99	// Rename changes the registered name of the dataset oldName to newName while
100	// keeping the dataset's exact position in the lineage graph: the node keeps
101	// its own direct upstream and downstream lists untouched, and every neighbor
102	// that referenced oldName now references newName in the same list position.
103	// No edge is added, removed, merged or reordered, and the total number of
104	// datasets in the graph is unchanged. Roots, leaves and intermediate datasets
105	// can all be renamed.
106	//
107	// The request is validated before the graph is touched, so a rejected rename
108	// leaves every node, edge and list order untouched. Names match by exact
109	// registered value (case-sensitive). An empty old or new name is rejected as
110	// a missing name; an oldName absent from the graph is rejected with an error
111	// naming it; a newName already registered to a different dataset is rejected
112	// with an error naming it. Renaming a dataset to its own current name is a
113	// successful no-op.
114	func Rename(graph map[string]*Lineage, oldName, newName string) error {
115		if oldName == "" {
116			return errInvalid("dataset name is required")
117		}
118		if newName == "" {
119			return errInvalid("new dataset name is required")
120		}
121		entry, ok := graph[oldName]
122		if !ok {
123			return errInvalid("dataset not found: " + oldName)
124		}
125		if oldName == newName {
126			return nil
127		}
128		if _, taken := graph[newName]; taken {
129			return errInvalid("dataset name already in use: " + newName)
130		}
131	
132		delete(graph, oldName)
133		entry.Dataset = newName
134		graph[newName] = entry
135	
136		// Rewire the reverse references in place: the renamed node keeps its slot
137		// in every neighbor's list, so each neighbor's ordering is preserved.
138		for _, parent := range entry.Parents {
139			children := graph[parent].Children
140			for i, child := range children {
141				if child == oldName {
142					children[i] = newName
143				}
144			}
145		}
146		for _, child := range entry.Children {
147			parents := graph[child].Parents
148			for i, parent := range parents {
149				if parent == oldName {
150					parents[i] = newName
151				}
152			}
153		}
154		return nil
155	}
156	
157	// Unregister removes a dataset registration from the lineage graph.
158	//
159	// Only a leaf dataset can be removed: a dataset with any direct downstream
160	// (a dataset still derived from it) is kept, regardless of how many upstreams
161	// it itself has. A removable dataset may still have direct upstreams; every
162	// one of them drops the dataset from its downstream list, in that list's
163	// original position, and the upstreams themselves and their other
164	// downstreams are untouched. A dataset with neither upstreams nor
165	// downstreams can also be removed. On success the name is gone from the
166	// graph: Impacts and Upstreams treat it as unregistered, and no empty node
167	// remains behind.
168	//
169	// The request is fully validated before the graph is touched, so a rejected
170	// removal leaves every node, edge and list order exactly as it was — no
171	// upstream can end up detached while the dataset stays. An empty name is
172	// rejected as a missing name; a non-empty name absent from the graph (also
173	// against an empty or nil graph) is rejected with an error naming it; a
174	// dataset that still has direct downstreams is rejected with an error that
175	// names it and states the remaining downstream. Names match by exact
176	// registered value (case-sensitive).
177	func Unregister(graph map[string]*Lineage, name string) error {
178		if name == "" {
179			return errInvalid("dataset name is required")
180		}
181		entry, ok := graph[name]
182		if !ok {
183			return errInvalid("dataset not found: " + name)
184		}
185		if len(entry.Children) > 0 {
186			return errInvalid("dataset " + name + " cannot be unregistered while it still has direct downstreams")
187		}
188	
189		// The dataset is a leaf, so its only edges point at its direct upstreams.
190		// Drop the matching reverse edge from each one, preserving the remaining
191		// order, then remove the node itself. The checks above guarantee nothing
192		// points back at it, so the graph stays fully consistent.
193		for _, parent := range entry.Parents {
194			if p, ok := graph[parent]; ok {
195				p.Children = removeChild(p.Children, name)
196			}
197		}
198		delete(graph, name)
199		return nil
200	}
201	
202	// ancestorProbe answers "can node reach target by following parent edges?" for
203	// many starting nodes against one fixed, read-only snapshot of the graph, i.e.
204	// whether target is among each node's direct or transitive upstreams. Each node
205	// in the shared ancestry is resolved at most once, so candidate parents that
206	// descend from a common source or merge along the way reuse the same findings
207	// instead of each paying for a complete traversal.
208	type ancestorProbe struct {
209		graph  map[string]*Lineage
210		target string
211		// resolved caches the conclusion for every fully explored node; visiting
212		// marks nodes mid-resolution. Register never accepts cycles, but visiting
213		// doubles as cycle protection regardless.
214		resolved map[string]bool
215		visiting map[string]bool
216	}
217	
218	func newAncestorProbe(graph map[string]*Lineage, target string) *ancestorProbe {
219		return &ancestorProbe{
220			graph:    graph,
221			target:   target,
222			resolved: map[string]bool{},
223			visiting: map[string]bool{},
224		}
225	}
226	
227	func (p *ancestorProbe) canReach(node string) bool {
228		if node == p.target {
229			return true
230		}
231		if hit, ok := p.resolved[node]; ok {
232			return hit
233		}
234		if p.visiting[node] {
235			return false
236		}
237		p.visiting[node] = true
238	
239		found := false
240		if entry, ok := p.graph[node]; ok {
241			for _, parent := range entry.Parents {
242				if p.canReach(parent) {
243					found = true
244					break
245				}
246			}
247		}
248		delete(p.visiting, node)
249		p.resolved[node] = found
250		return found
251	}
252	
253	// removeChild drops every occurrence of child from children, preserving the
254	// relative order of the remaining entries.
255	func removeChild(children []string, child string) []string {
256		out := children[:0]
257		for _, c := range children {
258			if c != child {
259				out = append(out, c)
260			}
261		}
262		return out
263	}
264	
265	// addChildOnce ensures child appears exactly once in children. An existing entry
266	// keeps its position (duplicate later entries are dropped); otherwise child is
267	// appended at the end.
268	func addChildOnce(children []string, child string) []string {
269		out := children[:0]
270		present := false
271		for _, c := range children {
272			if c == child {
273				if present {
274					continue
275				}
276				present = true
277			}
278			out = append(out, c)
279		}
280		if !present {
281			out = append(out, child)
282		}
283		return out
284	}
